statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and nine of the twenty-four hours published here contain no tradable Nasdaq-100 interval at all; the fifteen slots from the scheduled 22:00Z Sunday reopen onward carry conditional Tail readings between 10 and 13, all far below the block threshold. Stress is 36, moderate: the 50% US tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian goods is in force after trade talks collapsed, Canada has dated a dollar-for-dollar response to 8 September, a Monday US Treasury press conference on isolating Iran's economy is scheduled, the 30-year yield sits near a two-decade high around 5.27%, and crude has closed a second consecutive week higher. Confidence is 85, high: every level, yield, oil and calendar item was re-verified against primary sources this hour, but no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to observe.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, while the VIX settled at 14.89, down 6.0% and near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with application and infrastructure software up about 1.2% against a semiconductor group averaging roughly -0.7% and megacaps five up against three down. Cross-asset context stays in conflict: the long end sold off while the VIX fell and gold rose, which is a Stress and Confidence signature rather than the aligned amplifier stack that would justify a higher Tail. Tail is therefore held at its closed-venue floor for the nine shut hours and in the 10-13 band across the fifteen reopen hours, with the narrow evidence-based danger window placed on the reopen repricing interval from 22:00Z to 02:00Z rather than across the whole overnight session.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with fifteen reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through nine shut hours, then carries conditional readings between 10 and 13 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen, while live US tariffs on Canadian goods, a scheduled Monday Treasury announcement on isolating Iran, a two-decade-high long end and a second week of energy gains stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T13:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T12:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the fourteen hours after it sit inside the horizon while the first nine do not. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33% from a 29,213.17 prior close, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session and the close finished below the open, ending a five-day losing streak into a week in which the index still lost about 2%. The VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0%. Rates remain the loudest cross-asset channel: H.15 for 20 August shows the 2-year at 4.19%, the 5-year at 4.39%, the 10-year at 4.69% and the 30-year at 5.23%, and the long bond rose more than three basis points again on Friday to about 5.27%, its highest in nearly two decades, with Treasury buyback plans and fiscal supply cited as drivers. Energy closed a second consecutive week higher, WTI at $87.06 and Brent at $94.39, with Iran-related supply risk and a renewed Houthi threat to Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb traffic in the background. Three policy items are unpriced by any equity venue over the weekend: the 50% US tariff on about $20 billion of Canadian goods that took effect after three days of talks collapsed, Canada's dollar-for-dollar retaliation on steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper and electronics dated 8 September, and a Monday US Treasury press conference set to detail an economic-isolation plan for Iran. Shared Finviz cross-asset context, collected at 13:22Z and labelled delayed latest-session data, is consistent with that reading rather than with an aligned one-way regime: index futures modestly higher on the session, VIX futures lower, crude marginally higher, gold up 2.39%, Treasury futures lower across the curve and the semiconductor group negative against firm software. That is conflict, not alignment, so it raises Stress and lowers directional conviction rather than raising Tail. The week ahead is dense: Nvidia reports on Wednesday after the close, the July PCE report and the second GDP estimate land the same morning, and the Jackson Hole symposium runs from Thursday with the Fed Chair keynote on Friday. Those are checkpoints inside the top-level event calendar, not observed structure, and they do not move Tail before they print.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is partial: 19 hourly assessments are available, while the 21:00Z clock-hour on 22 August and the 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z clock-hours on 23 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress decayed steadily across the shut weekend, from 42 at the start of the window on Saturday afternoon down to 34 by Sunday morning, as the Canadian retaliation date and the Iran announcement moved from new information to known scheduled items. Confidence stayed in the 86-88 band, reflecting complete verified evidence for a closed venue rather than any live price path. The whole window is a market holiday for equity index futures, so none of these readings rests on observed Nasdaq-100 structure.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The following eight slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them, while Stress rises from 36 to 46 as the reopen approaches with the weekend information set unpriced. The final fifteen slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12 and the first full hour after it the horizon peak of 13, after which Tail decays through the Asian session to 10 as the base case assumes the reopen move is absorbed and volatility decays. It rebuilds modestly to 11-13 across the European session and the US pre-market as participation returns and the Monday catalyst set approaches. Every reading from 22:00Z onward is conditional: no reopen structure has been observed, and the readings would need revision if price extended repeatedly after failed retracements or held near a session extreme. Stress peaks at 49 around the reopen and again in the final horizon hour, staying in the elevated band for most of the tradable slots. The single scheduled US release inside the horizon is the medium-impact Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z; the US cash open at 13:30Z falls beyond it. The danger window is placed narrowly on the 22:00Z-02:00Z reopen repricing interval.
